bandReport.notes: Band covers items 41-60 with no gaps and no repeats. Item 41 begins cleanly at the top of p10-c1 and item 60 ends complete (all four options) at the foot of p13-c2, so nothing spills past either band edge. Three items straddle the gutter WITHIN a page and were assembled c1-then-c2 as instructed: item 49 (statements in p11-c1, the 'How many' line and options in p11-c2), item 53 (list in p12-c1, question line and options in p12-c2), item 58 (list in p13-c1, question line and options in p13-c2). All four column crops on all four pages are clean - the gutter was detected on every page (_render.json reports gutterFound true for indices 10-13) and no line is sliced, no item number is missing from the top of a c2, and no fragment of one column appears in the other. The only crop artefact is cosmetic: on p12 the printed page number 25 sits astride the gutter, so p12-c1 ends with a truncated '2' and p12-c2 begins with '25'; no question text is affected. Line-wrap hyphens were joined into whole words in five places (46(a) 'hydro-fluorocarbon' -> 'hydrofluorocarbon'; 52 II 'exis-tence' -> 'existence'; 55 III 'employ-ment' -> 'employment' and 'Funda-mental' -> 'Fundamental' in both right-hand cells; 56 II 'circum-stances' -> 'circumstances'). Genuine mid-line hyphens were kept ('Fuel cell-electric hybrid', 'man-made', 'high-energy', 'full-fledged', 'one-half', 'CL-20', 'LLM-105'). Items 52, 55 and 57 print genuine two-column pair grids and are rendered as GFM pipe tables with the separator row; the roman numerals stay inside the left cell exactly as printed. Item 58 statement I prints an EN DASH in 'List I-Union List'; transcribed with a plain ASCII hyphen to keep the field ASCII-safe - the reading is unambiguous. Likewise the curly quotes around Part 'C' in item 52 III and the apostrophe in 'Governor's office' (58 III) are transcribed as straight ASCII quotes. Verbatim oddity worth knowing before anyone 'corrects' it: item 55's right-hand cell for pair I is printed as 'The Directive Principles of the State Policy' - the booklet's own wording, with the extra 'the', not the usual 'Directive Principles of State Policy'. Item 56 is also unusual in shape: it says 'Consider the following statements :' and then prints a lead-in clause ('With reference to the Constitution of India, if an area in a State is declared as Scheduled Area under the Fifth Schedule') whose two roman items are grammatical continuations of it and carry no terminal full stops; both are reproduced exactly. Two subtopics are NOT from catalog.json and are offered for extension: item 52 uses 'Formation and Reorganization of States' (the item is about how Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland and Tripura came into being - no listed subtopic under Centre-State Relations and Federalism covers state creation) and item 57 uses 'Statutory Bodies and Administering Ministries' (the item maps three statutory boards to their Union Ministries; the listed 'Special Commissions' does not fit). Every subject and chapter is copied exactly from catalog.json and all nine are Paper I General Studies subjects. No question in this band contains mathematics, so there are no LaTeX zones. No answers are supplied anywhere in this file.
